questions.knowledge_point: Reducing a Quadratic Form to Canonical Form Using Lagrange's Method: 2D-Case
questions.problem:
Lagrange's method can be used to reduce the quadratic form $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}$ to the canonical form given below. 

$$
2{y}_{1}^{2}-\boxed{}\,{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=\boxed{} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what is missing from the blank spaces?
questions.worked_solution:
We apply Lagrange's method as follows:

First, we group ${x}_{1}^{2}$-term with all cross-product terms that contain ${x}_{1}$ and factor out the coefficient of ${x}_{1}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} & =2([{x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}]-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2(({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} & =2({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})^{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the canonical form is

$$
2{y}_{1}^{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the missing parts are as follows:

$\,$ $3\,$ and $\,{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Reducing a Quadratic Form to Canonical Form Using Lagrange's Method: 2D-Case
questions.problem:
Lagrange's method can be used to reduce the quadratic form $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}+9{x}_{2}^{2}-8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ to the canonical form given below. 

$$
2{y}_{1}^{2}+\boxed{}\,{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=\boxed{} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what is missing from the blank spaces?
questions.worked_solution:
We apply Lagrange's method as follows:

First, we group ${x}_{1}^{2}$-term with all cross-product terms that contain ${x}_{1}$ and factor out the coefficient of ${x}_{1}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+9{x}_{2}^{2}-8{x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\  & =(2{x}_{1}^{2}-8{x}_{1}{x}_{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2} & =2([{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}]-4{x}_{2}^{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2(({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2})+9{x}_{2}^{2} & =2({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})^{2}-8{x}_{2}^{2}+9{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the canonical form is

$$
2{y}_{1}^{2}+1{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the missing parts are as follows:

$\,$ $1\,$ and $\,{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}.$
